log.text: Light Screen up on P2's side
Light Screen ended on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Double TR lead: Farigiraf (Armor Tail blanks Prankster status, Sash guarantees TR) + Hatterene (Magic Bounce, LO-boosted spread). If Whimsicott Prankster-reverses TR, Hatterene resets it. Dual Dazzling Gleam pressures through Sash. Back: Kingambit cleans with Kowtow/Iron Head under TR; Mega Gardevoir Pixilate Hyper Voice sweeps.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent rain/speed team — Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/TR), Basculegion (Swift Swim Adaptability), Politoed (Drizzle), Tsareena (Queenly Majesty), Metagross, Ampharos (Mega). Our TR plan: Farigiraf's Armor Tail only blocks priority targeting us, not field moves like Tailwind/TR. Whimsicott can Prankster-TR to cancel ours; double setter lead hedges. Kingambit Iron Head 2HKO Whimsicott through Sash. Mega Gardevoir Pixilate Hyper Voice is primary Fairy offense.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott + Metagross to pressure either Trick Room setter immediately while retaining Tailwind and later Trick Room reversal. Politoed + Basculegion provide a strong rain endgame, weather control into Arcanine-Hisui, and Icy Wind as secondary speed control.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 selection: Whimsicott/Metagross lead, Politoed/Basculegion back. Preserve Metagross as the main Fairy answer and use it to pressure Hatterene or Farigiraf before Trick Room. Whimsicott can reverse established Trick Room on a later turn; do not rely on simultaneous Turn 1 Trick Room against a slower setter. Preserve Politoed for rain control against Arcanine-Hisui and to enable Basculegion’s late-game Wave Crash. Opposing Farigiraf’s Focus Sash means plan to combine chip with Metagross pressure. Watch Kingambit priority when Tsareena is not brought.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Hatterene)
decisions.rationale: Farigiraf sets Trick Room while Hatterene Protects. Metagross Meteor Mash OHKOs Hatterene (149-212%) but Farigiraf survives any single hit with Focus Sash. If Whimsicott Tailwinds, TR overrides; if Whimsicott TRs to cancel, Hatterene is safe and we can reset. This hedges both opponent options while preserving both setters.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent rain/speed team — Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/TR), Basculegion (Swift Swim Adaptability), Politoed (Drizzle), Tsareena (Queenly Majesty), Metagross, Ampharos (Mega). Our TR plan: Farigiraf's Armor Tail only blocks priority targeting us, not field moves like Tailwind/TR. Whimsicott can Prankster-TR to cancel ours; double setter lead hedges. Kingambit Iron Head 2HKO Whimsicott through Sash. Mega Gardevoir Pixilate Hyper Voice is primary Fairy offense. Metagross Meteor Mash OHKOs Hatterene; Farigiraf Sash survives any single hit. Kingambit takes 12-25% from Metagross Meteor Mash.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast breaks Farigiraf’s Focus Sash and adds chip for a later Metagross finish, while Meteor Mash threatens a guaranteed OHKO on Hatterene across legal bulk if it connects, removing the more dangerous Life Orb setter before Trick Room.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 selection: Whimsicott/Metagross lead, Politoed/Basculegion back. Preserve Metagross as the primary Fairy answer. Use Whimsicott’s Moonblast to break Farigiraf’s Focus Sash, then combine that chip with Metagross pressure. If Trick Room is established, look for a safe Whimsicott reversal while preserving Politoed for rain control and Basculegion’s late-game Wave Crash.

decisions.rationale: Under TR, both Hatterene (44) and Farigiraf (72) move before Whimsicott (149–184). Double Psychic into Whimsicott guarantees the KO before it can cancel Trick Room: Hatterene Psychic does 64.7–125.2%; if it doesn't OHKO, Sash leaves Whimsicott at 1 HP and Farigiraf Psychic (40.7–80%) finishes. Metagross likely OHKOs Hatterene with Meteor Mash, but TR stays up. We trade our sweeper for their speed control and keep the TR advantage with Farigiraf + bench.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent rain/speed team — Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/TR), Basculegion (Swift Swim Adaptability), Politoed (Drizzle), Tsareena (Queenly Majesty), Metagross (Expert Belt), Ampharos (Mega). Our TR plan: Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks priority targeting us (Bullet Punch, Aqua Jet, Sucker Punch) but not field moves. Metagross Meteor Mash OHKOs Hatterene (149–212%); Stomping Tantrum does 41–59%. Farigiraf Sash survives any single hit. Kingambit resists Steel, takes Metagross hits well. Mega Gardevoir Pixilate Hyper Voice is primary Fairy offense. Whimsicott is their only TR cancel; eliminating it preserves our speed control.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit is slower than Metagross (63 vs 90–122), moves first under TR. Kowtow Cleave is 2x into Metagross (58–122% range, possible OHKO). Kingambit resists Meteor Mash and is immune to Psychic; Stomping Tantrum does only 28–57%. Farigiraf stays in, preserving TR and threatening with Dazzling Gleam if a Fairy-weak foe switches in for Whimsicott.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: TR up 4 turns. Opponent rain/speed team — Whimsicott Prankster (fainted), Basculegion Swift Swim Adaptability, Politoed Drizzle, Tsareena Queenly Majesty, Metagross Expert Belt, Ampharos Mega. Our TR core: Farigiraf (Armor Tail blocks priority), Kingambit (Black Glasses), Gardevoir-Mega (Pixilate Hyper Voice). Light Screen 5 turns remaining. Hatterene fainted. Farigiraf Sash intact at 65%. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave 2x into Metagross (Steel no longer resists Dark Gen6+). Metagross Stomping Tantrum 2x into Kingambit but only 28–57%.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Metagross)
decisions.rationale: Light Screen sharply reduces the double-special pressure that could remove Whimsicott before it can later reverse Trick Room. Metagross targets Hatterene with its super-effective Meteor Mash, removing the stronger Life Orb attacker and secondary Trick Room setter if it connects.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 selection: Whimsicott/Metagross lead, Politoed/Basculegion back. Preserve Metagross as the primary Fairy answer. Farigiraf’s Focus Sash has been broken. Hatterene revealed Protect and Farigiraf revealed Trick Room. Prioritize removing Hatterene with Metagross, then seek a safe Whimsicott Trick Room reversal. Preserve Politoed for rain control and Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure.

decisions.rationale: Bring Politoed to exploit Trick Room with its lower Speed, preserve Basculegion as the late-game cleaner, and support Metagross through rain, Helping Hand, or speed control.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 brought Whimsicott/Metagross with Politoed/Basculegion. Farigiraf revealed Trick Room and Psychic; its Focus Sash was broken. Hatterene revealed Protect and Psychic. Preserve Metagross as the primary Fairy answer. Preserve Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure. Use Politoed for rain control and Helping Hand support.

decisions.rationale: Both our mons move first under TR. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave into Metagross: 78.9–134.1% with Supreme Overlord 1.1x, strong OHKO chance. Farigiraf Psychic chips Politoed ~20–34% through Light Screen. If Metagross falls, only Politoed attacks; Kingambit survives Weather Ball (43–77%). Opponent's best counter (Helping Hand + Stomping Tantrum) is neutralised if Metagross faints first.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: TR up 3 turns remaining after this. Rain 4 turns. Opponent Light Screen 4 turns. Our TR core: Farigiraf (Armor Tail blocks foe priority), Kingambit (Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord 1 fallen=1.1x), Gardevoir-Mega in back. Hatterene fainted. Opponent: Politoed Drizzle, Metagross Expert Belt, Basculegion Swift Swim Adaptability, Tsareena Queenly Majesty, Ampharos-Mega. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave OHKO range on Metagross ~79–134%. Metagross Stomping Tantrum + Expert Belt does 41–69% to Kingambit; with Helping Hand 62–103% — eliminate Metagross first. Gardevoir-Mega is faster than foes so moves last under TR; deploy after TR ends or as cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Kingambit with rain-boosted Weather Ball plus super-effective Expert Belt Stomping Tantrum. This is more reliable into bulky spreads than either attack alone and removes the largest immediate threat to Metagross; Farigiraf’s damage is mitigated by Light Screen.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 brought Whimsicott/Metagross with Politoed/Basculegion. Farigiraf revealed Trick Room and Psychic; its Focus Sash was broken. Hatterene revealed Protect and Psychic. Opponent’s Kingambit has Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord, and a Brave nature. Preserve Metagross as the primary Fairy answer when practical. Preserve Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure. Use Politoed for rain control and Helping Hand support.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double Basculegion to guarantee KO: Kowtow Cleave 89.9–169.7% + Psychic 20–36.9% (after Light Screen) = min 109.9%. Under TR Kingambit then Farigiraf move before both foes. Even if Politoed Helping Hands, Basculegion faints before attacking. Only risk is Basculegion Protect — but foe needs damage, unlikely to sacrifice attacking turn. If Basculegion falls, 2v1 vs Politoed wins.

Protect preserves Basculegion from Kingambit’s super-effective Kowtow Cleave while Politoed’s rain-boosted Weather Ball pressures the knockout after dealing 50% last turn. This punishes the likely attempt to remove Basculegion and avoids exposing it under Trick Room.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 brought Whimsicott/Metagross with Politoed/Basculegion. Farigiraf revealed Trick Room and Psychic; its Focus Sash was broken. Hatterene revealed Protect and Psychic. Kingambit has Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord, Brave nature, and revealed Kowtow Cleave. Farigiraf’s Armor Tail blocks opposing priority moves aimed at its side, so Aqua Jet cannot pressure either foe while it remains. Preserve Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure and use Politoed for rain control and Helping Hand support.

decisions.rationale: Under TR both our mons move first. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave (89.9–169.7%) + Farigiraf Psychic through Light Screen (15–27.7%) = 104.9% minimum, guaranteed KO on Basculegion before it acts. This removes Swift Swim before TR ends. Politoed can only KO one of our mons in return; Gardevoir-Mega cleans up the 2v1.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: TR ends after this turn. Rain 2 turns remaining. Opponent Light Screen 1 turn remaining after this. Our TR core: Farigiraf (Armor Tail), Kingambit (Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord 1 fallen=1.1x), Gardevoir-Mega in back. Hatterene fainted. Opponent: Politoed Drizzle, Basculegion Swift Swim Adaptability. Eliminate Basculegion first to neutralize rain speed; Gardevoir-Mega cleans Politoed after TR ends.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Weather Ball reliably finishes Kingambit through rain without Icy Wind’s miss chance. Basculegion must attempt consecutive Protect because either Kowtow Cleave or Psychic can remove it before it acts under Trick Room; preserving it gives a strong position once Trick Room expires.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 brought Whimsicott, Metagross, Politoed, and Basculegion. Opponent brought Farigiraf, Hatterene, and Kingambit, with the fourth unrevealed. Farigiraf revealed Trick Room and Psychic; its Focus Sash was broken. Hatterene revealed Protect and Psychic. Kingambit has Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord, Brave nature, and revealed Kowtow Cleave. Farigiraf’s Armor Tail blocks opposing priority aimed at its side, so Aqua Jet cannot pressure either foe while Farigiraf remains. Preserve Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure; use Politoed for rain control and Helping Hand support.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Gardevoir)
decisions.rationale: Set TR safely: Gardevoir Mega+Protect at +4 priority blocks Politoed's attack; Farigiraf TR at -7 goes last. Next turn no rain, no Light Screen, TR active — Farigiraf (72 Speed) moves first, Mega Gardevoir (100) follows. Double attack KOs lone Politoed. Avoids gambling on double Psychic through Light Screen with Farigiraf at risk of Weather Ball KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: TR core Farigiraf (Armor Tail, Focus Sash) + Gardevoir-Mega (Pixilate). Opponent down to lone Politoed. After TR reset, clean up with Farigiraf Psychic + Mega Gardevoir Pixilate Hyper Voice under TR. Rain and Light Screen expire this turn. Mega Gardevoir loses Drizzle but gains Pixilate for Fairy Hyper Voice STAB.

decisions.rationale: Use the final rain turn for maximum single-target damage into the already weakened Farigiraf. Light Screen improves Politoed's chance to survive both special attackers, while Protect would merely lose both rain and screen and Icy Wind sacrifices too much immediate pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 bring: Whimsicott, Metagross, Politoed, Basculegion. Opponent bring: Farigiraf, Hatterene, Kingambit, Gardevoir. Farigiraf revealed Trick Room and Psychic; Focus Sash was broken; Armor Tail blocks priority aimed at its side. Hatterene revealed Protect and Psychic. Kingambit revealed Kowtow Cleave; it is Brave with Black Glasses and Supreme Overlord. Gardevoir has Gardevoirite, Modest nature, Drizzle before Mega, and can Mega Evolve into Pixilate Gardevoir-Mega. Avoid consecutive Protect unless forced; Basculegion's second consecutive Protect failed and exposed it. Preserve Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure when possible; Politoed supplies rain and Helping Hand support.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room, Farigiraf (72 Spe) moves first, then Politoed (90–122), then Mega Gardevoir (138). Double Psychic into Politoed: Farigiraf 29–52% + Gardevoir 39–70% = 68–121% into 72% HP. Very high KO probability. Even if both roll low, Politoed survives with a sliver, acts once (Weather Ball likely KOs Farigiraf but Gardevoir tanks it), then Gardevoir finishes. No better play exists.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: TR core Farigiraf (Armor Tail, Focus Sash) + Gardevoir-Mega (Pixilate). Opponent's Politoed is Bold nature, Sitrus Berry consumed. Under TR, Farigiraf (72) always moves before Politoed (90–122), Gardevoir-Mega (138) moves after. Pixilate Hyper Voice is Fairy-type 108 BP STAB spread 0.75x; Psychic is stronger single-target. Focus Sash only activates from full HP — useless at 19%.

decisions.rationale: Weather Ball is the strongest accurate option into Farigiraf and should finish it based on the prior rain-boosted damage. Icy Wind risks a miss and its Speed drop benefits Gardevoir under Trick Room.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 bring: Whimsicott, Metagross, Politoed, Basculegion. Opponent bring: Farigiraf, Hatterene, Kingambit, Gardevoir. Farigiraf has Focus Sash, Armor Tail, Trick Room and Psychic. Hatterene has Life Orb, Magic Bounce, Protect and Psychic. Kingambit is Brave with Black Glasses and Supreme Overlord; revealed Kowtow Cleave. Gardevoir is Modest with Gardevoirite, revealed Drizzle before Mega Evolution and Protect after Mega Evolution; Mega Gardevoir can pressure with Pixilate Hyper Voice. Avoid consecutive Protect unless forced. Preserve Basculegion for late-game Adaptability Wave Crash/Last Respects pressure when possible; Politoed supplies rain and Helping Hand support.

reflections.summary: Trick Room from Farigiraf and Hatterene allowed slow, powerful attackers to move first and KO key threats before the opponent's fast rain offense could act, while the opponent lacked a way to stop or reverse Trick Room.
reflections.adjustment: Expect the opponent to bring Whimsicott's own Trick Room to cancel or Ampharos-Mega for a slow mode. Consider leading Hatterene to set Trick Room safely, preserving Farigiraf's Focus Sash for a mid-game reset, and be ready to play around a Trick Room cancel.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's rain team: Politoed (Bold, Sitrus Berry, Drizzle), Basculegion (Adamant, Mystic Water, Adaptability), Whimsicott (Timid, Focus Sash, Prankster, Trick Room, Tailwind, Light Screen, Moonblast), Metagross (Adamant, Expert Belt). Unrevealed: Ampharos-Mega (Modest, Ampharosite, likely Mold Breaker) and Tsareena (Adamant, Wide Lens, Queenly Majesty). Opponent may use Trick Room cancel or bring slow Ampharos-Mega next game. Our Trick Room core: Hatterene (Quiet, Life Orb, Magic Bounce) is slower than Farigiraf (Quiet, Focus Sash, Armor Tail) and moves first under Trick Room. Gardevoir-Mega (Modest, Pixilate) is fastest under Trick Room. Kingambit (Brave, Black Glasses, Supreme Overlord) gains boosts from fainted allies.

reflections.summary: The loss came from team preview: the non-Mega Whimsicott/Metagross/Politoed/Basculegion four was poorly matched into hard Trick Room. Tailwind and Basculegion’s priority lost value against Trick Room plus Armor Tail, Kingambit removed Metagross, and protected Mega Gardevoir benefited from Farigiraf resetting Trick Room.
reflections.adjustment: Do not repeat this four. Bench Basculegion for the slowest available Trick Room-resistant attacker and, if a viable Mega holder exists, bring and evolve it rather than conceding the Mega advantage. Preserve Focus Sash Whimsicott specifically to reverse Trick Room while attacking Farigiraf before it can reset.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors a hard Trick Room plan with multiple setters and Brave/Quiet attackers. Farigiraf may reset Trick Room beside a protecting Mega Gardevoir; double-target it through Focus Sash when possible. Armor Tail suppresses priority, making Basculegion a poor preview choice. Magic Bounce discourages status-based disruption into Hatterene. Kingambit aggressively pressures Metagross and Basculegion with Black Glasses Kowtow Cleave. Next plan: bring slower anti-Trick Room offense, preserve Whimsicott to reverse Trick Room, and prioritize an appropriate Mega option if available.
